text:
maria: quick heads-up — seeing p99 blow up in prod when concurrent requests > 800 :eyes:

maria: microbatch size set to 8 for the rollout, but on high concurrency the KV cache hit-rate drops from ~0.85 to ~0.45 and eviction rate spikes

dan: saw same in canary. flame graphs point to a lot of time in kv::lookup and lock contention. also kernel chooser falls back to generic matmul around the same time
kevin: perf snapshot from node-12: p95 220ms -> p95 260ms, p99 520ms -> 1.1s; kv evict/sec went from 3 -> 120
kevin: pasted profiling snippet:
```
# top stacks (node-12)
kv::lookup 48%
kernel_selector::choose_slow_path 22%
torch::matmul_generic 15%
scheduler::microbatch_flush 8%
```

maria: interesting signal: when we limit microbatch to 4 p99 improves but throughput drops ~18%

dan: could try gating microbatch size on instantaneous cache-hit ratio. if hit < 0.6 force mb=4 else allow 8

kevin: also probable hotkey thrash — a small set of prompts dominate and keep evicting each other. we might benefit from per-key sticky pinning or TTL bumping

maria: proposed plan:
- dan: prototype mb gate + metric (cache-hit 60s avg) in staging
- kevin: add per-key heatmap + count-based pinning opt in
- i'll run a scaled soak at 1k concurrent on staging tomorrow

infra-bot: deploy job #5421 queued by dan

dan: noted. will also add extra instrumentation: kv-hit histogram, eviction latency, kernel-choice histogram

kevin: if we can't stabilize with gating, then fallback is to make kernel selector prefer the more cache-friendly kernels even if peak throughput lower

maria: agreed. keep updates here. thanks :thumbsup:
